sections.label: Content note
sections.body: **Content note:** this page discusses abuse, neglect, restraint and the deaths of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. [Where to report abuse is listed below.](#kop-ri-report)

sections.label: Not the troubled teen industry
sections.heading: Not the troubled teen industry
sections.body:
Group homes and other residential services for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) are not part of the troubled teen industry. Kids Over Profits does not track these homes or list them in our directory. The people who live in them are adults, with a rights movement of their own, led by self-advocates.

We made this page because the two systems meet. Some of the same companies and private equity owners run both. Restraint, seclusion and drugs used to control behavior turn up in both. Some disabled young people grow up in youth programs and move into adult services. We are not the experts on this system: the self-advocates and organizations listed below are.

sections.label: What the industry is
sections.heading: What this system is
sections.body:
Most adults with IDD who get paid support live with family. On June 30, 2021, the newest national count, about 1.38 million people received long-term supports through state developmental disability agencies, and 63% of them lived in a relative's home. About 299,000 lived in a group home, another group setting or an intermediate care facility ([University of Minnesota, Residential Information Systems Project, FY 2021](https://ici-s.umn.edu/files/aaQxdJjAit/risp_2021_final_acc)).

Medicaid pays for nearly all of it. In fiscal year 2021, Medicaid home and community-based services (HCBS) waivers paid $47.1 billion for supports for 953,571 people with IDD. Intermediate Care Facilities for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF/IIDs), a Medicaid benefit with its own federal rules, cost $8.68 billion for 63,085 people ([RISP, FY 2021](https://ici-s.umn.edu/files/aaQxdJjAit/risp_2021_final_acc)).

Large state institutions have not all closed. On June 30, 2021, 106 state-run IDD facilities for 16 or more people were open, with an average of 15,049 residents a day, down from a peak of 194,650 in 1967. Eighteen states and the District of Columbia had none left ([RISP, FY 2021](https://ici-s.umn.edu/files/aaQxdJjAit/risp_2021_final_acc)).

Outside those institutions, private providers run almost every home under state contracts: of about 232,000 places where people with IDD lived outside a family home in 2021, 1,940 were run by states ([RISP](https://ici-s.umn.edu/files/aaQxdJjAit/risp_2021_final_acc)). Those providers were long mostly regional nonprofits and church groups. The Private Equity Stakeholder Project counted more than 1,000 private equity acquisitions of disability and elder care providers from 2013 to 2023 ([PESP, March 2025](https://pestakeholder.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/PESP_Report_IDD_2025.pdf)). Two of the largest operators have private equity owners:

- **Sevita**, formerly The MENTOR Network and Civitas Solutions, says it has [60,000 employees serving 70,000 people](https://www.sevitahealth.com/about-us/). Centerbridge Partners and The Vistria Group [bought it in March 2019](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1608638/000119312519069320/d713806dex992.htm).
- **BrightSpring Health Services**, formerly ResCare, owned [more than 600 residential facilities](https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/kendalltaggart/kkr-brightspring-disability-private-equity-abuse) when the private equity firm KKR took control in March 2019. It filed to [go public in January 2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1865782/000119312524000734/d251968ds1.htm).

sections.label: Where it meets the TTI
sections.heading: Where it meets the troubled teen industry
sections.body:
### The same companies

- **Sevita / The MENTOR Network** serves [adults and children with IDD and children in foster care](https://www.sevitahealth.com/about-us/). A 2017 Senate Finance Committee investigation of for-profit foster care [used The MENTOR Network as its case study](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CPRT-115SPRT26354/html/CPRT-115SPRT26354.htm) and, in the Committee's words, [raised concerns about treatment and deaths among foster children](https://www.finance.senate.gov/chairmans-news/grassley-wyden-probe-reports-of-abuse-at-group-homes-in-iowa-and-oregon) in its care. Its brand NeuroRestorative runs [14 group homes for young people in Illinois](/facility/neurorestorative-il/) that are in our records. In 2024 Florida moved to revoke NeuroRestorative's license there, citing its use of restraint and seclusion on children ([PESP, March 2025, p. 23](https://pestakeholder.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/PESP_Report_IDD_2025.pdf#page=24)).
- **ResCare / BrightSpring** called itself the nation's largest private provider of services for people with developmental disabilities in its [2011 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000776325/000110465912010518/a11-30009_110k.htm). The same report describes a Youth Services division: residential treatment for young people with emotional and behavioral issues and for juveniles in the justice system, foster care, and 14 Job Corps centers, residential programs for youth ages 16 to 24. BrightSpring still lists [foster care and youth services](https://www.brightspringhealth.com/services/family-youth-services/). Our records include two West Virginia youth programs under the ResCare name.
- **Devereux Advanced Behavioral Health**, a nonprofit, runs youth residential programs, [43 of them in our records](/operator/devereux-advanced-behavioral-health/). The Senate Finance Committee found it treats children with IDD in 12 specialized programs ([Senate Finance Committee, 2024, p. 23](https://www.finance.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/sfc_report_warehouses_of_neglect.pdf#page=23)). It also runs adult group homes: [more than 60 in New Jersey alone](https://www.devereux.org/site/SPageServer?pagename=nj_residential), for nearly 300 adults, and [adult IDD homes in Massachusetts](https://www.devereux.org/site/SPageServer?pagename=ma_adults).
- **The Judge Rotenberg Educational Center** in Canton, Massachusetts, [serves children and adults](https://www.disabilityscoop.com/2026/05/07/fda-may-finalize-ban-on-shock-devices-used-on-people-with-developmental-disabilities/31990/) with developmental disabilities and with behavioral and emotional problems. It is the only facility in the country known to use electric skin shock devices on the people in its care; the FDA estimated that about 50 people had treatment plans that included them ([FDA, March 2024](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/medical-devices-news-and-events/fda-proposes-new-ban-electrical-stimulation-devices-self-injurious-or-aggressive-behavior)). The FDA banned the devices in 2020. A federal appeals court vacated the ban in July 2021, Congress gave the FDA clear authority in the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act of 2022, and the FDA [proposed a new ban in March 2024](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/03/26/2024-06037/banned-devices-proposal-to-ban-electrical-stimulation-devices-for-self-injurious-or-aggressive). As of October 2026 no final rule had been published. [The center is in our records](/facility/judge-rotenberg-educational-center-ma/).

### The same practices

In 1999 the GAO linked 24 deaths in one year to restraint or seclusion in facilities for people with mental illness or what was then called mental retardation. At the time, federal rules covered restraint in ICFs and nursing homes, but not in psychiatric hospitals, children's residential centers or community group homes ([GAO, 1999](https://www.gao.gov/products/hehs-99-176)). Federal ICF/IID rules now allow drugs to control behavior only as part of a plan to stop the behavior, with team approval and a yearly attempt to withdraw them ([42 CFR 483.450](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/483.450)). In a 2024-25 survey across many states, 37% of adults with IDD in group settings took medication for "behavioral challenges", and only 55% of the adults taking it had a behavior plan ([National Core Indicators](https://idd.nationalcoreindicators.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/IPS-24-25-14-Medications.pdf)).

### From one system to the other

Children and teenagers with IDD are placed in youth residential programs, sometimes for most of their childhood. The Senate Finance Committee found Devereux stays of up to 6,928 days, almost 19 years, on its Florida campus ([2024, p. 103](https://www.finance.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/sfc_report_warehouses_of_neglect.pdf#page=103)). Its report also describes a 19-year-old autistic resident who died after a restraint at Laurel Heights, a Universal Health Services youth hospital in Georgia ([p. 59](https://www.finance.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/sfc_report_warehouses_of_neglect.pdf#page=59)). Several of the companies above run services on both sides of the age line, from youth programs to adult group homes.

sections.label: What investigations found
sections.heading: What investigations have found
sections.body:
- **Unreported injuries (HHS, 2016-2018).** Audits by the HHS Office of Inspector General found that group homes did not report 99% of critical incidents in Connecticut, 58% in Massachusetts and 95% in Maine to investigators. In one Massachusetts case a resident suffered head lacerations while aides restrained them. A January 2018 [joint report by the Inspector General, the Administration for Community Living and the Office for Civil Rights](https://oig.hhs.gov/documents/reports/10119/group-homes-joint-report.pdf) found media reports of health and safety problems in group homes in 49 states. The [state audits](https://oig.hhs.gov/reports/featured/group-homes/) are listed on the Inspector General's site.
- **The MENTOR Network (Senate, 2020).** Senate Finance Committee reports on two of its affiliates found that [REM Iowa](https://www.finance.senate.gov/download/report-on-investigation_-rem-iowa) had recurring critical incidents, including failures to report abuse or neglect, and that [MENTOR Oregon](https://www.finance.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/120220%20Life%20at%20Cypress%20House%20-%20An%20Examination%20of%20Care%20Provided%20by%20MENTOR%20Oregon.pdf) showed "a consistent pattern of substandard care" ([Committee summary](https://www.finance.senate.gov/ranking-members-news/grassley-wyden-issue-reports-on-developmental-disability-care-facilities-in-iowa-and-oregon)).
- **KKR and BrightSpring (BuzzFeed News, 2022).** In seven states, KKR owned 16% of the intermediate care facilities but received 40% of the most serious citations, more than 500, between March 2019 and the end of 2021. The company took out $1.1 billion in new loans and paid more than $135 million a year in interest ([BuzzFeed News](https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/kendalltaggart/kkr-brightspring-disability-private-equity-abuse)). KKR and BrightSpring disputed the findings.
- **Illinois (Chicago Tribune, 2016).** The "Suffering in Secret" series found more than 1,300 cases of documented harm in group homes and their day programs since July 2011, and at least 42 deaths linked to abuse or neglect, far more than the state had reported ([Nieman Foundation summary](https://nieman.harvard.edu/chicago-tribunes-suffering-in-secret-wins-50th-annual-worth-bingham-prize-for-investigative-journalism/)).
- **New York (The New York Times, 2011).** The ["Abused and Used" series](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/nyregion/abused-and-used-series-page.html) found that the state kept workers who had physically or sexually abused residents of its homes and rarely reported abuse allegations to law enforcement. The state then changed how workers accused of abuse are disciplined ([Columbia Journalism Review](https://www.cjr.org/the_kicker/times_series_on_group-home_abu.php)).

sections.label: Where to report abuse
sections.heading: Where to report abuse
sections.body:
- **If someone is in danger now**, call 911.
- **Adult Protective Services** takes reports of abuse, neglect and exploitation of adults with disabilities in most states. In some states a separate agency handles adults with developmental disabilities, or adults under 60. The National Adult Protective Services Association keeps [the reporting contact for every state and territory](https://www.napsa-now.org/help-in-your-area/).
- **The Eldercare Locator**, run by the federal government, refers callers to local agencies, mainly for older adults: call or text 1-800-677-1116, or visit [eldercare.acl.gov](https://eldercare.acl.gov/).
- **Protection and Advocacy agencies** are independent disability rights agencies in every state and territory. Find yours in the [National Disability Rights Network directory](https://www.ndrn.org/about/ndrn-member-agencies/).
- **Medicaid Fraud Control Units** investigate abuse and neglect of residents of health care facilities and board and care facilities, and of Medicaid enrollees in other settings ([HHS Office of Inspector General](https://oig.hhs.gov/fraud/medicaid-fraud-control-units-mfcu/)).
- Also tell the state agency that licenses the home or pays for the services.
- **988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline**, 24 hours: call or text [988](tel:988).

Our [reporting directory](/report-abuse/) lists agencies state by state.

sections.label: Organizations to learn from
sections.heading: Learn from the people who work on this
sections.body:
- [Self Advocates Becoming Empowered (SABE)](https://www.sabeusa.org/): The nationwide organization of self-advocates, people with intellectual and developmental disabilities speaking for themselves. Its priorities include closing institutions.
- [Autistic Self Advocacy Network (ASAN)](https://autisticadvocacy.org/about-asan/): A national disability rights organization run by and for autistic people.
- [ADAPT](https://adapt.org/): A grassroots disability rights group known for direct action for the right to live at home, not in nursing homes and institutions.
- [National Disability Rights Network (NDRN)](https://www.ndrn.org/about/): The membership organization for the Protection and Advocacy agencies and Client Assistance Programs in every state and territory.
- [The Arc of the United States](https://thearc.org/about-us/): Has advocated for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families since 1950, with chapters across the country.
- [National Council on Independent Living (NCIL)](https://www.ncil.org/about/): A cross-disability organization advocating for independent living and disability rights since 1982.

sections.label: Tell us if we got this wrong
sections.heading: Tell us if we got this wrong
sections.body: If you live or work in this system, or you are a self-advocate or a family member, and something on this page is wrong, please [tell us](/contact/). We will correct it.
